text:
Maria (CS): FYI - ACME reported an INT4 endpoint regression after yesterday's calibration push. p95 latency jumped ~2.5x and a few requests returned garbled tokens compared to FP16 baseline. Endpoint: acme-replies-int4, model v3.2. Customer is on prod traffic.
Ben - Runtime: Can you paste the exact payload and the sample prompts that showed garbled output? Also which GPU type are they on?
Maria (CS): They sent a repro snippet and logs. GPU: A10G. Sample prompt: "Summarize the following legal clause...". Payload (sanitized):
```
{"input": "Summarize the following legal clause: ...", "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0.0}
```
Carol - ML: Two quick hypothesis: 1) calibration produced overly aggressive scale factors causing saturation -> decoding errors, 2) kernel selection heuristics are choosing an INT4 kernel that's slower for this sequence length / batch pattern. We've seen similar A10G behavior when per-layer ranges are tiny.
Eli (SRE): I pulled the latest perf traces from the customer's host. Profiling snippet (filtered):
```
kernel: int4_attention_v2  | exec_ms: 2.7 | memcpy_ms: 1.6 | cpu_wait_ms: 3.4
kernel: fp16_attention     | exec_ms: 1.1 | memcpy_ms: 0.2 | cpu_wait_ms: 0.9
kv-cache: hit-rate 92% but lots of tiny batch flushes
```
Eli (SRE): The INT4 kernel is causing extra CPU-side waits and larger memcpy due to an alignment fallback path. That explains the latency regression.
Ben - Runtime: Ok that matches. Runtime is currently selecting int4_attention_v2 because the quantized metadata reports "supports_kv_cache=true" and sequence_length distribution matched the threshold. But the kernel has a slow memcpy path on A10G for odd token counts. Two mitigation paths: 1) force route ACME to fp16 until we patch kernel heuristics, or 2) toggle kernel to int4_attention_v1 (faster on A10G but slightly lower quality) + calibrate.
Maria (CS): Customer needs a fast fix. Preferably route to FP16 for now. Can we canary that? I'll message them.
Ben - Runtime: @oncall-bot can we push a routing override (fp16) for acme-replies-int4 as a 100% rollback?
oncall-bot: Deploy request received. Queuing a routing override. ETA ~10m. :gear:
deploy-bot: Canary policy created: acme-replies-int4 -> fp16 (100%) by customer_id=ACME.
Carol - ML: Simultaneously we should regenerate calibration using the corrected script. We've identified a bug where symmetric vs asymmetric mode got flipped for small per-channel ranges; that increases dequant ops and can cause both quality and perf issues. I have a PR with a fix and per-layer diagnostics.
Ben - Runtime: After canary, I'll add a temporary heuristic patch to prefer fp16 when batch_size <= 4 and sequence_len >= 64 on A10G. That should avoid the slow memcpy path while we roll out a kernel fix.
Maria (CS): Communicating rollback to ACME now: "We detected an issue with the int4 calibration and have temporarily routed your production traffic to FP16 while we apply a fix. Monitoring closely and will update in 30m." :white_check_mark:
Eli (SRE): Canary applied. Observing metrics: p95 dropped back to baseline within 2 minutes. No garbled tokens reported in the initial 50 samples. Telemetry snapshot:
```
before: p95=320ms, p50=85ms
canary(fp16): p95=120ms, p50=80ms
```
Ben - Runtime: Good. Action items: 1) Carol to land calibration fix and push new quant metadata (PR #2345). 2) Ben to land heuristic patch to kernel selector (PR #2346) and prepare kernel update. 3) Eli to keep routing override until we validate 24h of traffic. 4) Maria to send post-mortem to ACME and confirm if they want a permanent fp16 route or retry int4 after fix.
Carol - ML: PR #2345 ready for review, includes per-layer scale dump for debugging and an opt-in stricter range pruning mode. Perf regressions in our internal tests look resolved when using corrected calibration.
Ben - Runtime: I'll also add a temporary rollout flag that can be flipped per-customer so we don't need to route everyone to fp16.
Maria (CS): Customer acked the rollback and appreciates the quick fix. They've asked for a timeline to try int4 again; I'll offer ETA of 48-72 hours after we validate recalibration + canary.
Eli (SRE): Leaving the override in place. Will check back in 24h. Also saving profiler traces and attaching to the ticket.
Ben - Runtime: After we merge the selector and calibration fixes, we should run a canary that reintroduces int4 at 5% traffic with quality checks against a fixed prompt set. I'll add the test harness.
Maria (CS): Thanks team — I'll update the ACME ticket and set a follow-up meeting with their infra lead for tomorrow.
oncall-bot: Note: incident created INC-2026-int4-acme; owners assigned: Maria (CS), Ben - Runtime, Carol - ML, Eli (SRE).
Maria (CS): Closing loop here for now. Will post updates in this thread as we validate. :pray:
